units.leftText: The words of Nehemiah the son of Hacaliah.
units.rightText: These are the words of Nehemiah son of Hacaliah:

units.leftText: Hanani, one of my brothers, came, he and certain men out of Judah; and I asked them about the Jews who had escaped, who were left of the captivity, and concerning Jerusalem.
units.rightText: Hanani, one of my brothers, arrived with men from Judah. So I questioned them about the remnant of the Jews who had survived the exile, and also about Jerusalem.

units.leftText: They said to me, “The remnant who are left of the captivity there in the province are in great affliction and reproach. The wall of Jerusalem is also broken down, and its gates are burned with fire.”
units.rightText: And they told me, “The remnant who survived the exile are there in the province, in great trouble and disgrace. The wall of Jerusalem is broken down, and its gates have been burned with fire.”

units.leftText: When I heard these words, I sat down and wept, and mourned several days; and I fasted and prayed before the God of heaven,
units.rightText: When I heard these words, I sat down and wept. I mourned for days, fasting and praying before the God of heaven.

units.leftText: and said, “I beg you, LORD, the God of heaven, the great and awesome God who keeps covenant and loving kindness with those who love him and keep his commandments,
units.rightText: Then I said:
leftNotes: 1:5 When rendered in ALL CAPITAL LETTERS, “LORD” or “GOD” is the translation of God’s Proper Name (Hebrew “יהוה*”, usually pronounced Yahweh).

units.leftText: let your ear now be attentive and your eyes open, that you may listen to the prayer of your servant which I pray before you at this time, day and night, for the children of Israel your servants, while I confess the sins of the children of Israel which we have sinned against you. Yes, I and my father’s house have sinned.
units.rightText: let Your eyes be open and Your ears attentive to hear the prayer that I, Your servant, now pray before You day and night for Your servants, the Israelites.

units.leftText: We have dealt very corruptly against you, and have not kept the commandments, nor the statutes, nor the ordinances, which you commanded your servant Moses.
units.rightText: We have behaved corruptly against You and have not kept the commandments, statutes, and ordinances that You gave Your servant Moses.

units.leftText: “Remember, I beg you, the word that you commanded your servant Moses, saying, ‘If you trespass, I will scatter you among the peoples;
units.rightText: Remember, I pray, the word that You commanded Your servant Moses when You said, ‘If you are unfaithful, I will scatter you among the nations,

units.leftText: but if you return to me, and keep my commandments and do them, though your outcasts were in the uttermost part of the heavens, yet I will gather them from there, and will bring them to the place that I have chosen, to cause my name to dwell there.’
units.rightText: but if you return to Me and keep and practice My commandments, then even if your exiles have been banished to the farthest horizon, I will gather them from there and bring them to the place I have chosen as a dwelling for My Name.’
rightNotes: 1:9 Or to the extremity of the heavens
1:9 Deuteronomy 30:1–4|DEU 30:1-4*

units.leftText: “Now these are your servants and your people, whom you have redeemed by your great power and by your strong hand.
units.rightText: They are Your servants and Your people. You redeemed them by Your great power and mighty hand.

units.leftText: Lord, I beg you, let your ear be attentive now to the prayer of your servant, and to the prayer of your servants who delight to fear your name; and please prosper your servant today, and grant him mercy in the sight of this man.”
units.rightText: O Lord, may Your ear be attentive to my prayer and to the prayers of Your servants who delight to revere Your name. Give Your servant success this day, I pray, and grant him mercy in the sight of this man.”
rightNotes: 1:11 Literally to the prayer of Your servant and to the prayer of Your servants

units.leftText: In the month Nisan, in the twentieth year of Artaxerxes the king, when wine was before him, I picked up the wine, and gave it to the king. Now I had not been sad before in his presence.
units.rightText: Now in the month of Nisan, in the twentieth year of King Artaxerxes, when wine was set before him, I took the wine and gave it to the king. I had never been sad in his presence,
rightNotes: 2:1 Nisan is the first month of the Hebrew lunar calendar, usually occurring within the months of March and April.

units.leftText: The king said to me, “Why is your face sad, since you are not sick? This is nothing else but sorrow of heart.”
units.rightText: so the king said to me, “Why is your face sad, though you are not ill? This could only be sadness of the heart.”

units.leftText: I said to the king, “Let the king live forever! Why shouldn’t my face be sad, when the city, the place of my fathers’ tombs, lies waste, and its gates have been consumed with fire?”
units.rightText: and replied to the king, “May the king live forever! Why should I not be sad when the city where my fathers are buried lies in ruins, and its gates have been destroyed by fire?”

units.leftText: Then the king said to me, “What is your request?”
units.rightText: “What is your request?” replied the king.

units.leftText: I said to the king, “If it pleases the king, and if your servant has found favor in your sight, I ask that you would send me to Judah, to the city of my fathers’ tombs, that I may build it.”
units.rightText: and answered the king, “If it pleases the king, and if your servant has found favor in your sight, I ask that you send me to Judah, to the city where my fathers are buried, so that I may rebuild it.”

units.leftText: The king said to me (the queen was also sitting by him), “How long will your journey be? When will you return?”
units.rightText: Then the king, with the queen seated beside him, asked me, “How long will your journey take, and when will you return?” So it pleased the king to send me, and I set a time.

units.leftText: Moreover I said to the king, “If it pleases the king, let letters be given me to the governors beyond the River, that they may let me pass through until I come to Judah;
units.rightText: I also said to him, “If it pleases the king, may letters be given to me for the governors west of the Euphrates, so that they will grant me safe passage until I reach Judah.
rightNotes: 2:7 Hebrew beyond the River; also in verse 9

units.leftText: and a letter to Asaph the keeper of the king’s forest, that he may give me timber to make beams for the gates of the citadel by the temple, for the wall of the city, and for the house that I will occupy.”
units.rightText: And may I have a letter to Asaph, keeper of the king’s forest, so that he will give me timber to make beams for the gates of the citadel to the temple, for the city wall, and for the house I will occupy.”

units.leftText: Then I came to the governors beyond the River, and gave them the king’s letters. Now the king had sent captains of the army and horsemen with me.
units.rightText: Then I went to the governors west of the Euphrates and gave them the king’s letters. The king had also sent army officers and cavalry with me.

units.leftText: When Sanballat the Horonite and Tobiah the Ammonite servant heard of it, it grieved them exceedingly, because a man had come to seek the welfare of the children of Israel.
units.rightText: But when Sanballat the Horonite and Tobiah the Ammonite official heard about this, they were deeply disturbed that someone had come to seek the well-being of the Israelites.

units.leftText: So I came to Jerusalem, and was there three days.
units.rightText: After I had arrived in Jerusalem and had been there three days,

units.leftText: I arose in the night, I and a few men with me. I didn’t tell anyone what my God put into my heart to do for Jerusalem. There wasn’t any animal with me except the animal that I rode on.
units.rightText: I set out at night with a few men. I did not tell anyone what my God had laid on my heart to do for Jerusalem. The only animal with me was the one on which I was riding.

units.leftText: I went out by night by the valley gate toward the jackal’s well, then to the dung gate; and I inspected the walls of Jerusalem, which were broken down, and its gates were consumed with fire.
units.rightText: So I went out at night through the Valley Gate toward the Well of the Serpent and the Dung Gate, and I inspected the walls of Jerusalem that had been broken down and the gates that had been destroyed by fire.
rightNotes: 2:13 Or Dragon or Jackal

units.leftText: Then I went on to the spring gate and to the king’s pool, but there was no place for the animal that was under me to pass.
units.rightText: Then I went on to the Fountain Gate and the King’s Pool, but there was no room for the animal under me to get through;

units.leftText: Then I went up in the night by the brook and inspected the wall; and I turned back, and entered by the valley gate, and so returned.
units.rightText: so I went up the valley by night and inspected the wall. Then I headed back and reentered through the Valley Gate.

units.leftText: The rulers didn’t know where I went, or what I did. I had not as yet told it to the Jews, nor to the priests, nor to the nobles, nor to the rulers, nor to the rest who did the work.
units.rightText: The officials did not know where I had gone or what I was doing, for I had not yet told the Jews or priests or nobles or officials or any other workers.

units.leftText: Then I said to them, “You see the bad situation that we are in, how Jerusalem lies waste, and its gates are burned with fire. Come, let’s build up the wall of Jerusalem, that we won’t be disgraced.”
units.rightText: Then I said to them, “You see the trouble we are in. Jerusalem lies in ruins, and its gates have been burned down. Come, let us rebuild the wall of Jerusalem, so that we will no longer be a disgrace.”

units.leftText: I told them about the hand of my God which was good on me, and also about the king’s words that he had spoken to me.
units.rightText: I also told them about the gracious hand of my God upon me, and what the king had said to me.

units.leftText: But when Sanballat the Horonite, Tobiah the Ammonite servant, and Geshem the Arabian, heard it, they ridiculed us and despised us, and said, “What is this thing that you are doing? Will you rebel against the king?”
units.rightText: But when Sanballat the Horonite, Tobiah the Ammonite official, and Geshem the Arab heard about this, they mocked us and ridiculed us, saying, “What is this you are doing? Are you rebelling against the king?”

units.leftText: Then I answered them, and said to them, “The God of heaven will prosper us. Therefore we, his servants, will arise and build; but you have no portion, nor right, nor memorial in Jerusalem.”
units.rightText: So I answered them and said, “The God of heaven is the One who will grant us success. We, His servants, will start rebuilding, but you have no portion, right, or claim in Jerusalem.”

units.leftText: Then Eliashib the high priest rose up with his brothers the priests, and they built the sheep gate. They sanctified it, and set up its doors. They sanctified it even to the tower of Hammeah, to the tower of Hananel.
units.rightText: At the Sheep Gate, Eliashib the high priest and his fellow priests began rebuilding. They dedicated it and installed its doors. After building as far as the Tower of the Hundred and the Tower of Hananel, they dedicated the wall.

units.leftText: Next to him the men of Jericho built. Next to them Zaccur the son of Imri built.
units.rightText: The men of Jericho built next to Eliashib, and Zaccur son of Imri built next to them.

units.leftText: The sons of Hassenaah built the fish gate. They laid its beams, and set up its doors, its bolts, and its bars.
units.rightText: The Fish Gate was rebuilt by the sons of Hassenaah. They laid its beams and installed its doors, bolts, and bars.

units.leftText: Next to them, Meremoth the son of Uriah, the son of Hakkoz made repairs. Next to them, Meshullam the son of Berechiah, the son of Meshezabel made repairs. Next to them, Zadok the son of Baana made repairs.
units.rightText: Next to them, Meremoth son of Uriah, the son of Hakkoz, made repairs. Next to him, Meshullam son of Berechiah, the son of Meshezabel, made repairs; and next to him, Zadok son of Baana made repairs as well.

units.leftText: Next to them, the Tekoites made repairs; but their nobles didn’t put their necks to the Lord’s work.
units.rightText: Next to him, the Tekoites made repairs, but their nobles did not put their shoulders to the work under their supervisors.
rightNotes: 3:5 Or their Lord or the governor

units.leftText: Joiada the son of Paseah and Meshullam the son of Besodeiah repaired the old gate. They laid its beams and set up its doors, its bolts, and its bars.
units.rightText: The Jeshanah Gate was repaired by Joiada son of Paseah and Meshullam son of Besodeiah. They laid its beams and installed its doors, bolts, and bars.
rightNotes: 3:6 Or The Old City Gate

units.leftText: Next to them, Melatiah the Gibeonite and Jadon the Meronothite, the men of Gibeon and of Mizpah, repaired the residence of the governor beyond the River.
units.rightText: Next to them, repairs were made by Melatiah the Gibeonite, Jadon the Meronothite, and the men of Gibeon and Mizpah, who were under the authority of the governor of the region west of the Euphrates.
rightNotes: 3:7 Hebrew the governor beyond the River

units.leftText: Next to him, Uzziel the son of Harhaiah, goldsmiths, made repairs. Next to him, Hananiah, one of the perfumers, made repairs, and they fortified Jerusalem even to the wide wall.
units.rightText: Next to them, Uzziel son of Harhaiah, one of the goldsmiths, made repairs. And next to him, Hananiah, one of the perfumers, made repairs. They fortified Jerusalem as far as the Broad Wall.

units.leftText: Next to them, Rephaiah the son of Hur, the ruler of half the district of Jerusalem, made repairs.
units.rightText: Next to them, Rephaiah son of Hur, ruler of a half-district of Jerusalem, made repairs;

units.leftText: Next to them, Jedaiah the son of Harumaph made repairs across from his house. Next to him, Hattush the son of Hashabneiah made repairs.
units.rightText: next to him, Jedaiah son of Harumaph made repairs across from his house; and next to him, Hattush son of Hashabneiah made repairs.

units.leftText: Malchijah the son of Harim and Hasshub the son of Pahathmoab repaired another portion and the tower of the furnaces.
units.rightText: Malchijah son of Harim and Hasshub son of Pahath-moab repaired another section, as well as the Tower of the Ovens.

units.leftText: Next to him, Shallum the son of Hallohesh, the ruler of half the district of Jerusalem, he and his daughters made repairs.
units.rightText: And next to them, Shallum son of Hallohesh, ruler of the other half-district of Jerusalem, made repairs, with the help of his daughters.

units.leftText: Hanun and the inhabitants of Zanoah repaired the valley gate. They built it, and set up its doors, its bolts, and its bars, and one thousand cubits of the wall to the dung gate.
units.rightText: The Valley Gate was repaired by Hanun and the residents of Zanoah. They rebuilt it, installed its doors, bolts, and bars, and repaired a thousand cubits of the wall as far as the Dung Gate.
leftNotes: 3:13 A cubit is the length from the tip of the middle finger to the elbow on a man’s arm, or about 18 inches or 46 centimeters.
rightNotes: 3:13 1,000 cubits is approximately 1,500 feet or 457.2 meters.

units.leftText: Malchijah the son of Rechab, the ruler of the district of Beth Haccherem, repaired the dung gate. He built it, and set up its doors, its bolts, and its bars.
units.rightText: The Dung Gate was repaired by Malchijah son of Rechab, ruler of the district of Beth-haccherem. He rebuilt it and installed its doors, bolts, and bars.

units.leftText: Shallun the son of Colhozeh, the ruler of the district of Mizpah, repaired the spring gate. He built it, covered it, and set up its doors, its bolts, and its bars; and he repaired the wall of the pool of Shelah by the king’s garden, even to the stairs that go down from David’s city.
units.rightText: The Fountain Gate was repaired by Shallun son of Col-hozeh, ruler of the district of Mizpah. He rebuilt it, roofed it, and installed its doors, bolts, and bars. He also repaired the wall of the Pool of Shelah near the king’s garden, as far as the stairs that descend from the City of David.
rightNotes: 3:15 Hebrew; Syriac Shallum
3:15 Pool of Shelah is another name for the Pool of Siloam.

units.leftText: After him, Nehemiah the son of Azbuk, the ruler of half the district of Beth Zur, made repairs to the place opposite the tombs of David, and to the pool that was made, and to the house of the mighty men.
units.rightText: Beyond him, Nehemiah son of Azbuk, ruler of a half-district of Beth-zur, made repairs up to a point opposite the tombs of David, as far as the artificial pool and the House of the Mighty.

units.leftText: After him, the Levites—Rehum the son of Bani made repairs. Next to him, Hashabiah, the ruler of half the district of Keilah, made repairs for his district.
units.rightText: Next to him, the Levites made repairs under Rehum son of Bani, and next to him, Hashabiah, ruler of a half-district of Keilah, made repairs for his district.

units.leftText: After him, their brothers, Bavvai the son of Henadad, the ruler of half the district of Keilah made repairs.
units.rightText: Next to him, their countrymen made repairs under Binnui son of Henadad, ruler of the other half-district of Keilah.
rightNotes: 3:18 Two Hebrew manuscripts and Syriac (see also LXX and Nehemiah 3:24|NEH 3:24*); most Hebrew manuscripts Bavvai

units.leftText: Next to him, Ezer the son of Jeshua, the ruler of Mizpah, repaired another portion across from the ascent to the armory at the turning of the wall.
units.rightText: And next to him, Ezer son of Jeshua, ruler of Mizpah, repaired another section opposite the ascent to the armory, near the angle in the wall.

units.leftText: After him, Baruch the son of Zabbai earnestly repaired another portion, from the turning of the wall to the door of the house of Eliashib the high priest.
units.rightText: Next to him, Baruch son of Zabbai diligently repaired another section, from the angle to the doorway of the house of Eliashib the high priest.

units.leftText: After him, Meremoth the son of Uriah the son of Hakkoz repaired another portion, from the door of the house of Eliashib even to the end of the house of Eliashib.
units.rightText: Next to him, Meremoth son of Uriah, the son of Hakkoz, repaired another section, from the doorway of the house of Eliashib to the end of the house.

units.leftText: After him, the priests, the men of the surrounding area made repairs.
units.rightText: And next to him, the priests from the surrounding area made repairs.

units.leftText: After them, Benjamin and Hasshub made repairs across from their house. After them, Azariah the son of Maaseiah the son of Ananiah made repairs beside his own house.
units.rightText: Beyond them, Benjamin and Hasshub made repairs in front of their house, and next to them, Azariah son of Maaseiah, the son of Ananiah, made repairs beside his house.

units.leftText: After him, Binnui the son of Henadad repaired another portion, from the house of Azariah to the turning of the wall, and to the corner.
units.rightText: After him, Binnui son of Henadad repaired another section, from the house of Azariah to the angle and the corner,

units.leftText: Palal the son of Uzai made repairs opposite the turning of the wall, and the tower that stands out from the upper house of the king, which is by the court of the guard. After him Pedaiah the son of Parosh made repairs.
units.rightText: and Palal son of Uzai made repairs opposite the angle and the tower that juts out from the upper palace of the king near the courtyard of the guard. Next to him, Pedaiah son of Parosh

units.leftText: (Now the temple servants lived in Ophel, to the place opposite the water gate toward the east, and the tower that stands out.)
units.rightText: and the temple servants living on the hill of Ophel made repairs opposite the Water Gate toward the east and the tower that juts out.
rightNotes: 3:26 Hebrew the Nethinim; also in verse 31

units.leftText: After him the Tekoites repaired another portion, opposite the great tower that stands out, and to the wall of Ophel.
units.rightText: And next to them, the Tekoites repaired another section, from a point opposite the great tower that juts out to the wall of Ophel.

units.leftText: Above the horse gate, the priests made repairs, everyone across from his own house.
units.rightText: Above the Horse Gate, each of the priests made repairs in front of his own house.

units.leftText: After them, Zadok the son of Immer made repairs across from his own house. After him, Shemaiah the son of Shecaniah, the keeper of the east gate, made repairs.
units.rightText: Next to them, Zadok son of Immer made repairs opposite his house, and next to him, Shemaiah son of Shecaniah, the guard of the East Gate, made repairs.

units.leftText: After him, Hananiah the son of Shelemiah, and Hanun, the sixth son of Zalaph, repaired another portion. After him, Meshullam the son of Berechiah made repairs across from his room.
units.rightText: Next to him, Hananiah son of Shelemiah, as well as Hanun the sixth son of Zalaph, repaired another section. Next to them, Meshullam son of Berechiah made repairs opposite his own quarters.

units.leftText: After him, Malchijah, one of the goldsmiths to the house of the temple servants, and of the merchants, made repairs opposite the gate of Hammiphkad and to the ascent of the corner.
units.rightText: Next to him, Malchijah, one of the goldsmiths, made repairs as far as the house of the temple servants and the merchants, opposite the Inspection Gate, and as far as the upper room above the corner.

units.leftText: Between the ascent of the corner and the sheep gate, the goldsmiths and the merchants made repairs.
units.rightText: And between the upper room above the corner and the Sheep Gate, the goldsmiths and merchants made repairs.

units.leftText: But when Sanballat heard that we were building the wall, he was angry, and was very indignant, and mocked the Jews.
units.rightText: Now when Sanballat heard that we were rebuilding the wall, he was furious and filled with indignation. He ridiculed the Jews

units.leftText: He spoke before his brothers and the army of Samaria, and said, “What are these feeble Jews doing? Will they fortify themselves? Will they sacrifice? Will they finish in a day? Will they revive the stones out of the heaps of rubbish, since they are burned?”
units.rightText: before his associates and the army of Samaria, saying, “What are these feeble Jews doing? Can they restore the wall by themselves? Will they offer sacrifices? Will they complete it in a day? Can they bring these burnt stones back to life from the mounds of rubble?”
rightNotes: 4:2 Or Will they commit themselves to God?

units.leftText: Now Tobiah the Ammonite was by him, and he said, “What they are building, if a fox climbed up it, he would break down their stone wall.”
units.rightText: Then Tobiah the Ammonite, who was beside him, said, “If even a fox were to climb up on what they are building, it would break down their wall of stones!”

units.leftText: “Hear, our God, for we are despised. Turn back their reproach on their own head. Give them up for a plunder in a land of captivity.
units.rightText: Hear us, O God, for we are despised. Turn their scorn back upon their own heads, and let them be taken as plunder to a land of captivity.

units.leftText: Don’t cover their iniquity. Don’t let their sin be blotted out from before you; for they have insulted the builders.”
units.rightText: Do not cover up their iniquity or let their sin be blotted out from Your sight, for they have provoked the builders.
rightNotes: 4:5 Or have provoked You to anger before the builders

units.leftText: So we built the wall; and all the wall was joined together to half its height, for the people had a mind to work.
units.rightText: So we rebuilt the wall until all of it was joined together up to half its height, for the people had a mind to work.

units.leftText: But when Sanballat, Tobiah, the Arabians, the Ammonites, and the Ashdodites heard that the repairing of the walls of Jerusalem went forward, and that the breaches began to be filled, they were very angry;
units.rightText: When Sanballat and Tobiah, together with the Arabs, Ammonites, and Ashdodites, heard that the repair to the walls of Jerusalem was progressing and that the gaps were being closed, they were furious,

units.leftText: and they all conspired together to come and fight against Jerusalem, and to cause confusion among us.
units.rightText: and all of them conspired to come and fight against Jerusalem and create a hindrance.

units.leftText: But we made our prayer to our God, and set a watch against them day and night because of them.
units.rightText: So we prayed to our God and posted a guard against them day and night.

units.leftText: Judah said, “The strength of the bearers of burdens is fading and there is much rubble, so that we are not able to build the wall.”
units.rightText: Meanwhile, the people of Judah said:
rightNotes: 4:10 Or Meanwhile, Judah said

units.leftText: Our adversaries said, “They will not know or see, until we come in among them and kill them, and cause the work to cease.”
units.rightText: And our enemies said, “Before they know or see a thing, we will come into their midst, kill them, and put an end to the work.”

units.leftText: When the Jews who lived by them came, they said to us ten times from all places, “Wherever you turn, they will attack us.”
units.rightText: At that time the Jews who lived nearby came and told us ten times over, “Wherever you turn, they will attack us.”

units.leftText: Therefore I set guards in the lowest parts of the space behind the wall, in the open places. I set the people by family groups with their swords, their spears, and their bows.
units.rightText: So I stationed men behind the lowest sections of the wall, at the vulnerable areas. I stationed them by families with their swords, spears, and bows.

units.leftText: I looked, and rose up, and said to the nobles, to the rulers, and to the rest of the people, “Don’t be afraid of them! Remember the Lord, who is great and awesome, and fight for your brothers, your sons, your daughters, your wives, and your houses.”
units.rightText: After I had made an inspection, I stood up and said to the nobles, the officials, and the rest of the people, “Do not be afraid of them. Remember the Lord, who is great and awesome, and fight for your brothers, your sons and your daughters, your wives and your homes.”

units.leftText: When our enemies heard that it was known to us, and God had brought their counsel to nothing, all of us returned to the wall, everyone to his work.
units.rightText: When our enemies heard that we were aware of their scheme and that God had frustrated it, each of us returned to his own work on the wall.

units.leftText: From that time forth, half of my servants did the work, and half of them held the spears, the shields, the bows, and the coats of mail; and the rulers were behind all the house of Judah.
units.rightText: And from that day on, half of my servants did the work while the other half held spears, shields, bows, and armor.

units.leftText: Those who built the wall, and those who bore burdens loaded themselves; everyone with one of his hands did the work, and with the other held his weapon.
units.rightText: who were rebuilding the wall. The laborers who carried materials worked with one hand and held a weapon with the other.

units.leftText: Among the builders, everyone wore his sword at his side, and so built. He who sounded the trumpet was by me.
units.rightText: And each of the builders worked with his sword strapped at his side. But the trumpeter stayed beside me.

units.leftText: I said to the nobles, and to the rulers and to the rest of the people, “The work is great and widely spread out, and we are separated on the wall, far from one another.
units.rightText: Then I said to the nobles, the officials, and the rest of the people: “The work is great and extensive, and we are spread out far from one another along the wall.

units.leftText: Wherever you hear the sound of the trumpet, rally there to us. Our God will fight for us.”
units.rightText: Wherever you hear the sound of the horn, rally to us there. Our God will fight for us!”

units.leftText: So we did the work. Half of the people held the spears from the rising of the morning until the stars appeared.
units.rightText: So we continued the work, while half of the men held spears from the break of dawn until the stars came out.

units.leftText: Likewise at the same time I said to the people, “Let everyone with his servant lodge within Jerusalem, that in the night they may be a guard to us, and may labor in the day.”
units.rightText: At that time I also said to the people, “Let every man and his servant spend the night inside Jerusalem, so that they can stand guard by night and work by day.”

units.leftText: So neither I, nor my brothers, nor my servants, nor the men of the guard who followed me took off our clothes. Everyone took his weapon to the water.
units.rightText: So neither I nor my brothers nor my servants nor the guards with me changed out of our clothes; each carried his weapon, even to go for water.
rightNotes: 4:23 Or each carried his weapon in his right hand

units.leftText: Then there arose a great cry of the people and of their wives against their brothers the Jews.
units.rightText: About that time there was a great outcry from the people and their wives against their fellow Jews.

units.leftText: For there were some who said, “We, our sons and our daughters, are many. Let us get grain, that we may eat and live.”
units.rightText: Some were saying, “We and our sons and daughters are numerous. We must get grain in order to eat and stay alive.”

units.leftText: There were also some who said, “We are mortgaging our fields, our vineyards, and our houses. Let us get grain, because of the famine.”
units.rightText: Others were saying, “We are mortgaging our fields, our vineyards, and our homes to get grain during the famine.”

units.leftText: There were also some who said, “We have borrowed money for the king’s tribute using our fields and our vineyards as collateral.
units.rightText: Still others were saying, “We have borrowed money to pay the king’s tax on our fields and vineyards.

units.leftText: Yet now our flesh is as the flesh of our brothers, our children as their children. Behold, we bring our sons and our daughters into bondage to be servants, and some of our daughters have been brought into bondage. It is also not in our power to help it, because other men have our fields and our vineyards.”
units.rightText: We and our children are just like our countrymen and their children, yet we are subjecting our sons and daughters to slavery. Some of our daughters are already enslaved, but we are powerless to redeem them because our fields and vineyards belong to others.”
leftNotes: 5:5 “Behold”, from “הִנֵּה*”, means look at, take notice, observe, see, or gaze at. It is often used as an interjection.

units.leftText: I was very angry when I heard their cry and these words.
units.rightText: When I heard their outcry and these complaints, I became extremely angry,

units.leftText: Then I consulted with myself, and contended with the nobles and the rulers, and said to them, “You exact usury, everyone of his brother.” I held a great assembly against them.
units.rightText: and after serious thought I rebuked the nobles and officials, saying, “You are exacting usury from your own brothers!”

units.leftText: I said to them, “We, after our ability, have redeemed our brothers the Jews that were sold to the nations; and would you even sell your brothers, and should they be sold to us?” Then they held their peace, and found not a word to say.
units.rightText: and said, “We have done our best to buy back our Jewish brothers who were sold to foreigners, but now you are selling your own brothers, that they may be sold back to us!”

units.leftText: Also I said, “The thing that you do is not good. Shouldn’t you walk in the fear of our God because of the reproach of the nations, our enemies?
units.rightText: So I continued, “What you are doing is not right. Shouldn’t you walk in the fear of our God to avoid the reproach of our foreign enemies?

units.leftText: I likewise, my brothers and my servants, lend them money and grain. Please let us stop this usury.
units.rightText: I, as well as my brothers and my servants, have been lending the people money and grain. Please, let us stop this usury.

units.leftText: Please restore to them, even today, their fields, their vineyards, their olive groves, and their houses, also the hundredth part of the money, and of the grain, the new wine, and the oil, that you are charging them.”
units.rightText: Please restore to them immediately their fields, vineyards, olive groves, and houses, along with the percentage of the money, grain, new wine, and oil that you have been assessing them.”

units.leftText: Then they said, “We will restore them, and will require nothing of them. We will do so, even as you say.”
units.rightText: “We will restore it,” they replied, “and will require nothing more from them. We will do as you say.”

units.leftText: Also I shook out my lap, and said, “So may God shake out every man from his house, and from his labor, that doesn’t perform this promise; even may he be shaken out and emptied like this.”
units.rightText: I also shook out the folds of my robe and said, “May God likewise shake out of his house and possessions every man who does not keep this promise. May such a man be shaken out and have nothing!”

units.leftText: Moreover from the time that I was appointed to be their governor in the land of Judah, from the twentieth year even to the thirty-second year of Artaxerxes the king, that is, twelve years, I and my brothers have not eaten the bread of the governor.
units.rightText: Furthermore, from the day King Artaxerxes appointed me to be their governor in the land of Judah, from his twentieth year until his thirty-second year (twelve years total), neither I nor my brothers ate the food allotted to the governor.

units.leftText: But the former governors who were before me were supported by the people, and took bread and wine from them, plus forty shekels of silver; yes, even their servants ruled over the people, but I didn’t do so, because of the fear of God.
units.rightText: The governors before me had heavily burdened the people, taking from them bread and wine plus forty shekels of silver. Their servants also oppressed the people. But I did not do this, because of my fear of God.
leftNotes: 5:15 A shekel is about 10 grams or about 0.35 ounces.
rightNotes: 5:15 40 shekels is approximately 1 pound or 453.6 grams of silver.

units.leftText: Yes, I also continued in the work of this wall. We didn’t buy any land. All my servants were gathered there to the work.
units.rightText: Instead, I devoted myself to the construction of the wall, and all my servants were gathered there for the work; we did not acquire any land.

units.leftText: Moreover there were at my table, of the Jews and the rulers, one hundred fifty men, in addition to those who came to us from among the nations that were around us.
units.rightText: There were 150 Jews and officials at my table, besides the guests from the surrounding nations.

units.leftText: Now that which was prepared for one day was one ox and six choice sheep. Also fowls were prepared for me, and once in ten days a store of all sorts of wine. Yet for all this, I didn’t demand the governor’s pay, because the bondage was heavy on this people.
units.rightText: Each day one ox, six choice sheep, and some fowl were prepared for me, and once every ten days an abundance of all kinds of wine was provided. But I did not demand the food allotted to the governor, because the burden on the people was so heavy.

units.leftText: Remember me, my God, for all the good that I have done for this people.
units.rightText: Remember me favorably, O my God, for all that I have done for this people.

units.leftText: Now when it was reported to Sanballat, Tobiah, Geshem the Arabian, and to the rest of our enemies that I had built the wall, and that there was no breach left in it (though even to that time I had not set up the doors in the gates),
units.rightText: When Sanballat, Tobiah, Geshem the Arab, and the rest of our enemies heard that I had rebuilt the wall and not a gap was left— though to that time I had not yet installed the doors in the gates—

units.leftText: Sanballat and Geshem sent to me, saying, “Come! Let’s meet together in the villages in the plain of Ono.” But they intended to harm me.
units.rightText: Sanballat and Geshem sent me this message: “Come, let us meet together in one of the villages on the plain of Ono.”
rightNotes: 6:2 Or in Kephirim
6:2 Or in the valley

units.leftText: I sent messengers to them, saying, “I am doing a great work, so that I can’t come down. Why should the work cease while I leave it and come down to you?”
units.rightText: So I sent messengers to them, saying, “I am doing a great work and cannot come down. Why should the work stop while I leave it to go down to you?”

units.leftText: They sent to me four times like this; and I answered them the same way.
units.rightText: Four times they sent me the same message, and each time I gave the same reply.

units.leftText: Then Sanballat sent his servant to me the same way the fifth time with an open letter in his hand,
units.rightText: The fifth time, Sanballat sent me this same message by his young servant, who had in his hand an unsealed letter

units.leftText: in which was written, “It is reported among the nations, and Gashmu says it, that you and the Jews intend to rebel. Because of that, you are building the wall. You would be their king, according to these words.
units.rightText: that read:

units.leftText: You have also appointed prophets to proclaim of you at Jerusalem, saying, ‘There is a king in Judah!’ Now it will be reported to the king according to these words. Come now therefore, and let’s take counsel together.”
units.rightText: and you have even appointed prophets in Jerusalem to proclaim on your behalf: ‘There is a king in Judah.’ Soon these rumors will reach the ears of the king. So come, let us confer together.”

units.leftText: Then I sent to him, saying, “There are no such things done as you say, but you imagine them out of your own heart.”
units.rightText: Then I sent him this reply: “There is nothing to these rumors you are spreading; you are inventing them in your own mind.”

units.leftText: For they all would have made us afraid, saying, “Their hands will be weakened from the work, that it not be done.” But now, strengthen my hands.
units.rightText: For they were all trying to frighten us, saying, “Their hands will be weakened in the work, and it will never be finished.”

units.leftText: I went to the house of Shemaiah the son of Delaiah the son of Mehetabel, who was shut in at his home; and he said, “Let us meet together in God’s house, within the temple, and let’s shut the doors of the temple; for they will come to kill you. Yes, in the night they will come to kill you.”
units.rightText: Later, I went to the house of Shemaiah son of Delaiah, the son of Mehetabel, who was confined to his house. He said:

units.leftText: I said, “Should a man like me flee? Who is there that, being such as I, would go into the temple to save his life? I will not go in.”
units.rightText: But I replied, “Should a man like me run away? Should one like me go into the temple to save his own life? I will not go!”

units.leftText: I discerned, and behold, God had not sent him, but he pronounced this prophecy against me. Tobiah and Sanballat had hired him.
units.rightText: I realized that God had not sent him, but that he had uttered this prophecy against me because Tobiah and Sanballat had hired him.

units.leftText: He was hired so that I would be afraid, do so, and sin, and that they might have material for an evil report, that they might reproach me.
units.rightText: He had been hired to intimidate me so that I would sin by doing as he suggested, so they could give me a bad name in order to discredit me.

units.leftText: “Remember, my God, Tobiah and Sanballat according to these their works, and also the prophetess Noadiah and the rest of the prophets that would have put me in fear.”
units.rightText: O my God, remember Tobiah and Sanballat for what they have done, and also Noadiah the prophetess and the other prophets who tried to intimidate me.

units.leftText: So the wall was finished in the twenty-fifth day of Elul, in fifty-two days.
units.rightText: So the wall was completed in fifty-two days, on the twenty-fifth of Elul.
rightNotes: 6:15 Elul is the sixth month of the Hebrew lunar calendar, usually occurring within the months of August and September.

units.leftText: When all our enemies heard of it, all the nations that were around us were afraid, and they lost their confidence; for they perceived that this work was done by our God.
units.rightText: When all our enemies heard about this, all the surrounding nations were afraid and disheartened, for they realized that this task had been accomplished by our God.

units.leftText: Moreover in those days the nobles of Judah sent many letters to Tobiah, and Tobiah’s letters came to them.
units.rightText: Also in those days, the nobles of Judah sent many letters to Tobiah, and Tobiah’s letters kept coming to them.

units.leftText: For there were many in Judah sworn to him because he was the son-in-law of Shecaniah the son of Arah; and his son Jehohanan had taken the daughter of Meshullam the son of Berechiah as wife.
units.rightText: For many in Judah were bound by oath to him, since he was a son-in-law of Shecaniah son of Arah, and his son Jehohanan had married the daughter of Meshullam son of Berechiah.

units.leftText: Also they spoke of his good deeds before me, and reported my words to him. Tobiah sent letters to put me in fear.
units.rightText: Moreover, these nobles kept reporting to me Tobiah’s good deeds, and they relayed my words to him. And Tobiah sent letters to intimidate me.

units.leftText: Now when the wall was built and I had set up the doors, and the gatekeepers and the singers and the Levites were appointed,
units.rightText: When the wall had been rebuilt and I had set the doors in place, the gatekeepers, singers, and Levites were appointed.

units.leftText: I put my brother Hanani, and Hananiah the governor of the fortress, in charge of Jerusalem; for he was a faithful man and feared God above many.
units.rightText: Then I put my brother Hanani in charge of Jerusalem, along with Hananiah the commander of the fortress, because he was a faithful man who feared God more than most.

units.leftText: I said to them, “Don’t let the gates of Jerusalem be opened until the sun is hot; and while they stand guard, let them shut the doors, and you bar them; and appoint watches of the inhabitants of Jerusalem, everyone in his watch, with everyone near his house.”
units.rightText: And I told them, “Do not open the gates of Jerusalem until the sun is hot. While the guards are on duty, keep the doors shut and securely fastened. And appoint the residents of Jerusalem as guards, some at their posts and some at their own homes.”

units.leftText: Now the city was wide and large; but the people were few therein, and the houses were not built.
units.rightText: Now the city was large and spacious, but there were few people in it, and the houses had not yet been rebuilt.

units.leftText: My God put into my heart to gather together the nobles, and the rulers, and the people, that they might be listed by genealogy. I found the book of the genealogy of those who came up at the first, and I found this written in it:
units.rightText: Then my God put it into my heart to assemble the nobles, the officials, and the people to be enrolled by genealogy. I found the genealogical register of those who had first returned, and I found the following written in it:

units.leftText: So the priests, the Levites, the gatekeepers, the singers, some of the people, the temple servants, and all Israel lived in their cities.
units.rightText: So the priests, Levites, gatekeepers, singers, and temple servants, along with some of the people and the rest of the Israelites, settled in their own towns. And by the seventh month the Israelites had settled in their towns.

units.leftText: All the people gathered themselves together as one man into the wide place that was in front of the water gate; and they spoke to Ezra the scribe to bring the book of the law of Moses, which the LORD had commanded to Israel.
units.rightText: At that time all the people gathered together in the square before the Water Gate, and they asked Ezra the scribe to bring out the Book of the Law of Moses, which the LORD had commanded for Israel.

units.leftText: Ezra the priest brought the law before the assembly, both men and women, and all who could hear with understanding, on the first day of the seventh month.
units.rightText: On the first day of the seventh month, Ezra the priest brought the Law before the assembly of men and women and all who could listen and understand.

units.leftText: He read from it before the wide place that was in front of the water gate from early morning until midday, in the presence of the men and the women, and of those who could understand. The ears of all the people were attentive to the book of the law.
units.rightText: So Ezra read it aloud from daybreak until noon as he faced the square before the Water Gate, in front of the men and women and those who could understand.

units.leftText: Ezra the scribe stood on a pulpit of wood, which they had made for the purpose; and beside him stood Mattithiah, Shema, Anaiah, Uriah, Hilkiah, and Maaseiah, on his right hand; and on his left hand, Pedaiah, Mishael, Malchijah, Hashum, Hashbaddanah, Zechariah, and Meshullam.
units.rightText: Ezra the scribe stood on a high wooden platform built for this occasion. At his right side stood Mattithiah, Shema, Anaiah, Uriah, Hilkiah, and Maaseiah, and at his left were Pedaiah, Mishael, Malchijah, Hashum, Hash-baddanah, Zechariah, and Meshullam.

units.leftText: Ezra opened the book in the sight of all the people (for he was above all the people), and when he opened it, all the people stood up.
units.rightText: Ezra opened the book in full view of all the people, since he was standing above them all, and as he opened it, all the people stood up.

units.leftText: Then Ezra blessed the LORD, the great God.
units.rightText: Then Ezra blessed the LORD, the great God, and with their hands uplifted, all the people said, “Amen, Amen!” Then they bowed down and worshiped the LORD with their faces to the ground.

units.leftText: Also Jeshua, Bani, Sherebiah, Jamin, Akkub, Shabbethai, Hodiah, Maaseiah, Kelita, Azariah, Jozabad, Hanan, Pelaiah, and the Levites, caused the people to understand the law; and the people stayed in their place.
units.rightText: The Levites — Jeshua, Bani, Sherebiah, Jamin, Akkub, Shabbethai, Hodiah, Maaseiah, Kelita, Azariah, Jozabad, Hanan, and Pelaiah — instructed the people in the Law as they stood in their places.

units.leftText: They read in the book, in the law of God, distinctly; and they gave the sense, so that they understood the reading.
units.rightText: So they read from the Book of the Law of God, explaining it and giving insight, so that the people could understand what was being read.
rightNotes: 8:8 Or translating it or paragraph by paragraph

units.leftText: Nehemiah, who was the governor, Ezra the priest and scribe, and the Levites who taught the people said to all the people, “Today is holy to the LORD your God. Don’t mourn, nor weep.” For all the people wept when they heard the words of the law.
units.rightText: Nehemiah the governor, Ezra the priest and scribe, and the Levites who were instructing the people said to all of them, “This day is holy to the LORD your God. Do not mourn or weep.”

units.leftText: Then he said to them, “Go your way. Eat the fat, drink the sweet, and send portions to him for whom nothing is prepared, for today is holy to our Lord. Don’t be grieved, for the joy of the LORD is your strength.”
units.rightText: Then Nehemiah told them, “Go and eat what is rich, drink what is sweet, and send out portions to those who have nothing prepared, since today is holy to our Lord. Do not grieve, for the joy of the LORD is your strength.”

units.leftText: So the Levites calmed all the people, saying, “Hold your peace, for the day is holy. Don’t be grieved.”
units.rightText: And the Levites calmed all the people, saying, “Be still, since today is holy. Do not grieve.”

units.leftText: All the people went their way to eat, to drink, to send portions, and to celebrate, because they had understood the words that were declared to them.
units.rightText: Then all the people began to eat and drink, to send out portions, and to rejoice greatly, because they understood the words that had been made known to them.

units.leftText: On the second day, the heads of fathers’ households of all the people, the priests, and the Levites were gathered together to Ezra the scribe, to study the words of the law.
units.rightText: On the second day of the month, the heads of all the families, along with the priests and Levites, gathered around Ezra the scribe to study the words of the Law.

units.leftText: They found written in the law how the LORD had commanded by Moses that the children of Israel should dwell in booths in the feast of the seventh month;
units.rightText: And they found written in the Law, which the LORD had commanded through Moses, that the Israelites were to dwell in booths during the feast of the seventh month,
rightNotes: 8:14 Or tabernacles or shelters; also in verses 15, 16, and 17

units.leftText: and that they should publish and proclaim in all their cities and in Jerusalem, saying, “Go out to the mountain, and get olive branches, branches of wild olive, myrtle branches, palm branches, and branches of thick trees, to make temporary shelters, as it is written.”
units.rightText: and that they should proclaim this message and spread it throughout their towns and in Jerusalem, saying, “Go out to the hill country and bring back branches of olive, wild olive, myrtle, palm, and other leafy trees, to make booths, as it is written.”
rightNotes: 8:15 Or pine; literally oil tree

units.leftText: So the people went out and brought them, and made themselves temporary shelters, everyone on the roof of his house, in their courts, in the courts of God’s house, in the wide place of the water gate, and in the wide place of Ephraim’s gate.
units.rightText: And the people went out, brought back branches, and made booths on their own rooftops, in their courtyards, in the courts of the house of God, and in the squares by the Water Gate and by the Gate of Ephraim.

units.leftText: All the assembly of those who had come back out of the captivity made temporary shelters and lived in the temporary shelters, for since the days of Joshua the son of Nun to that day the children of Israel had not done so. There was very great gladness.
units.rightText: The whole assembly that had returned from exile made booths and lived in them. From the days of Joshua son of Nun until that day, the Israelites had not celebrated like this. And there was great rejoicing.
rightNotes: 8:17 Hebrew Jeshua, a variant of Joshua

units.leftText: Also day by day, from the first day to the last day, he read in the book of the law of God. They kept the feast seven days; and on the eighth day was a solemn assembly, according to the ordinance.
units.rightText: Day after day, from the first day to the last, Ezra read from the Book of the Law of God. The Israelites kept the feast for seven days, and on the eighth day they held an assembly, according to the ordinance.

units.leftText: Now in the twenty-fourth day of this month the children of Israel were assembled with fasting, with sackcloth, and dirt on them.
units.rightText: On the twenty-fourth day of the same month, the Israelites gathered together, fasting and wearing sackcloth, with dust on their heads.

units.leftText: The offspring of Israel separated themselves from all foreigners and stood and confessed their sins and the iniquities of their fathers.
units.rightText: Those of Israelite descent separated themselves from all the foreigners, and they stood and confessed their sins and the iniquities of their fathers.

units.leftText: They stood up in their place, and read in the book of the law of the LORD their God a fourth part of the day; and a fourth part they confessed and worshiped the LORD their God.
units.rightText: While they stood in their places, they read from the Book of the Law of the LORD their God for a quarter of the day, and they spent another quarter of the day in confession and worship of the LORD their God.

units.leftText: Then Jeshua, Bani, Kadmiel, Shebaniah, Bunni, Sherebiah, Bani, and Chenani of the Levites stood up on the stairs, and cried with a loud voice to the LORD their God.
units.rightText: And the Levites — Jeshua, Bani, Kadmiel, Shebaniah, Bunni, Sherebiah, Bani, and Chenani — stood on the raised platform and cried out in a loud voice to the LORD their God.

units.leftText: Then the Levites, Jeshua, and Kadmiel, Bani, Hashabneiah, Sherebiah, Hodiah, Shebaniah, and Pethahiah, said, “Stand up and bless the LORD your God from everlasting to everlasting! Blessed be your glorious name, which is exalted above all blessing and praise!
units.rightText: Then the Levites— Jeshua, Kadmiel, Bani, Hashabneiah, Sherebiah, Hodiah, Shebaniah, and Pethahiah— said, “Stand up and bless the LORD your God from everlasting to everlasting:

units.leftText: You are the LORD, even you alone. You have made heaven, the heaven of heavens, with all their army, the earth and all things that are on it, the seas and all that is in them, and you preserve them all. The army of heaven worships you.
units.rightText: You alone are the LORD.

units.leftText: You are the LORD, the God who chose Abram, brought him out of Ur of the Chaldees, gave him the name of Abraham,
units.rightText: You are the LORD,

units.leftText: found his heart faithful before you, and made a covenant with him to give the land of the Canaanite, the Hittite, the Amorite, the Perizzite, the Jebusite, and the Girgashite, to give it to his offspring, and have performed your words, for you are righteous.
units.rightText: You found his heart faithful before You,

units.leftText: “You saw the affliction of our fathers in Egypt, and heard their cry by the Red Sea,
units.rightText: You saw the affliction of our fathers in Egypt;

units.leftText: and showed signs and wonders against Pharaoh, against all his servants, and against all the people of his land, for you knew that they dealt proudly against them, and made a name for yourself, as it is today.
units.rightText: You performed signs and wonders against Pharaoh,

units.leftText: You divided the sea before them, so that they went through the middle of the sea on the dry land; and you cast their pursuers into the depths, as a stone into the mighty waters.
units.rightText: You divided the sea before them,

units.leftText: Moreover, in a pillar of cloud you led them by day; and in a pillar of fire by night, to give them light in the way in which they should go.
units.rightText: You led them with a pillar of cloud by day

units.leftText: “You also came down on Mount Sinai, and spoke with them from heaven, and gave them right ordinances and true laws, good statutes and commandments,
units.rightText: You came down on Mount Sinai

units.leftText: and made known to them your holy Sabbath, and commanded them commandments, statutes, and a law, by Moses your servant,
units.rightText: You revealed to them Your holy Sabbath

units.leftText: and gave them bread from the sky for their hunger, and brought water out of the rock for them for their thirst, and commanded them that they should go in to possess the land which you had sworn to give them.
units.rightText: In their hunger You gave them bread from heaven;

units.leftText: “But they and our fathers behaved proudly, hardened their neck, didn’t listen to your commandments,
units.rightText: But they and our fathers became arrogant and stiff-necked

units.leftText: and refused to obey. They weren’t mindful of your wonders that you did among them, but hardened their neck, and in their rebellion appointed a captain to return to their bondage. But you are a God ready to pardon, gracious and merciful, slow to anger, and abundant in loving kindness, and didn’t forsake them.
units.rightText: They refused to listen and failed to remember

units.leftText: Yes, when they had made themselves a molded calf, and said, ‘This is your God who brought you up out of Egypt,’ and had committed awful blasphemies,
units.rightText: Even when they cast for themselves

units.leftText: yet you in your manifold mercies didn’t forsake them in the wilderness. The pillar of cloud didn’t depart from over them by day, to lead them in the way; neither did the pillar of fire by night, to show them light, and the way in which they should go.
units.rightText: You in Your great compassion

units.leftText: You gave also your good Spirit to instruct them, and didn’t withhold your manna from their mouth, and gave them water for their thirst.
units.rightText: You gave Your good Spirit to instruct them.

units.leftText: “Yes, forty years you sustained them in the wilderness. They lacked nothing. Their clothes didn’t grow old, and their feet didn’t swell.
units.rightText: For forty years You sustained them in the wilderness,

units.leftText: Moreover you gave them kingdoms and peoples, which you allotted according to their portions. So they possessed the land of Sihon, even the land of the king of Heshbon, and the land of Og king of Bashan.
units.rightText: You gave them kingdoms and peoples

units.leftText: You also multiplied their children as the stars of the sky, and brought them into the land concerning which you said to their fathers that they should go in to possess it.
units.rightText: You multiplied their descendants

units.leftText: “So the children went in and possessed the land; and you subdued before them the inhabitants of the land, the Canaanites, and gave them into their hands, with their kings and the peoples of the land, that they might do with them as they pleased.
units.rightText: So their descendants went in and possessed the land;

units.leftText: They took fortified cities and a rich land, and possessed houses full of all good things, cisterns dug out, vineyards, olive groves, and fruit trees in abundance. So they ate, were filled, became fat, and delighted themselves in your great goodness.
units.rightText: They captured fortified cities and fertile land

units.leftText: “Nevertheless they were disobedient and rebelled against you, cast your law behind their back, killed your prophets that testified against them to turn them again to you, and they committed awful blasphemies.
units.rightText: But they were disobedient and rebelled against You;

units.leftText: Therefore you delivered them into the hand of their adversaries, who distressed them. In the time of their trouble, when they cried to you, you heard from heaven; and according to your manifold mercies you gave them saviors who saved them out of the hands of their adversaries.
units.rightText: So You delivered them into the hands

units.leftText: But after they had rest, they did evil again before you; therefore you left them in the hands of their enemies, so that they had the dominion over them; yet when they returned and cried to you, you heard from heaven; and many times you delivered them according to your mercies,
units.rightText: But as soon as they had rest,

units.leftText: and testified against them, that you might bring them again to your law. Yet they were arrogant, and didn’t listen to your commandments, but sinned against your ordinances (which if a man does, he shall live in them), turned their backs, stiffened their neck, and would not hear.
units.rightText: You admonished them to turn back to Your law,

units.leftText: Yet many years you put up with them, and testified against them by your Spirit through your prophets. Yet they would not listen. Therefore you gave them into the hand of the peoples of the lands.
units.rightText: You were patient with them for many years,

units.leftText: “Nevertheless in your manifold mercies you didn’t make a full end of them, nor forsake them; for you are a gracious and merciful God.
units.rightText: But in Your great compassion,

units.leftText: Now therefore, our God, the great, the mighty, and the awesome God, who keeps covenant and loving kindness, don’t let all the travail seem little before you that has come on us, on our kings, on our princes, on our priests, on our prophets, on our fathers, and on all your people, since the time of the kings of Assyria to this day.
units.rightText: So now, our God, the great and mighty and awesome God

units.leftText: However you are just in all that has come on us; for you have dealt truly, but we have done wickedly.
units.rightText: You are just in all that has befallen us,

units.leftText: Also our kings, our princes, our priests, and our fathers have not kept your law, nor listened to your commandments and your testimonies with which you testified against them.
units.rightText: Our kings and leaders and priests and fathers

units.leftText: For they have not served you in their kingdom, and in your great goodness that you gave them, and in the large and rich land which you gave before them. They didn’t turn from their wicked works.
units.rightText: For even while they were in their kingdom,

units.leftText: “Behold, we are servants today, and as for the land that you gave to our fathers to eat its fruit and its good, behold, we are servants in it.
units.rightText: So here we are today as slaves

units.leftText: It yields much increase to the kings whom you have set over us because of our sins. Also they have power over our bodies and over our livestock, at their pleasure, and we are in great distress.
units.rightText: Its abundant harvest goes to the kings

units.leftText: Yet for all this, we make a sure covenant, and write it; and our princes, our Levites, and our priests, seal it.”
units.rightText: In view of all this, we make a binding agreement, putting it in writing and sealing it with the names of our leaders, Levites, and priests.”
rightNotes: 9:38 Hebrew does not include the names of.

units.rightText: Seraiah, Azariah, Jeremiah,

units.leftText: Pashhur, Amariah, Malchijah,
units.rightText: Pashhur, Amariah, Malchijah,

units.rightText: Hattush, Shebaniah, Malluch,

units.leftText: Harim, Meremoth, Obadiah,
units.rightText: Harim, Meremoth, Obadiah,

units.rightText: Daniel, Ginnethon, Baruch,

units.leftText: Meshullam, Abijah, Mijamin,
units.rightText: Meshullam, Abijah, Mijamin,

units.rightText: Maaziah, Bilgai, and Shemaiah.

units.rightText: The Levites:

units.leftText: and their brothers, Shebaniah, Hodiah, Kelita, Pelaiah, Hanan,
units.rightText: and their associates: Shebaniah, Hodiah, Kelita, Pelaiah, Hanan,

units.leftText: Mica, Rehob, Hashabiah,
units.rightText: Mica, Rehob, Hashabiah,

units.leftText: Zaccur, Sherebiah, Shebaniah,
units.rightText: Zaccur, Sherebiah, Shebaniah,

units.leftText: Hodiah, Bani, and Beninu.
units.rightText: Hodiah, Bani, and Beninu.

units.leftText: The chiefs of the people: Parosh, Pahathmoab, Elam, Zattu, Bani,
units.rightText: And the leaders of the people:

units.leftText: Bunni, Azgad, Bebai,
units.rightText: Bunni, Azgad, Bebai,

units.leftText: Adonijah, Bigvai, Adin,
units.rightText: Adonijah, Bigvai, Adin,

units.leftText: Ater, Hezekiah, Azzur,
units.rightText: Ater, Hezekiah, Azzur,

units.leftText: Hodiah, Hashum, Bezai,
units.rightText: Hodiah, Hashum, Bezai,

units.leftText: Hariph, Anathoth, Nobai,
units.rightText: Hariph, Anathoth, Nebai,

units.leftText: Magpiash, Meshullam, Hezir,
units.rightText: Magpiash, Meshullam, Hezir,

units.leftText: Meshezabel, Zadok, Jaddua,
units.rightText: Meshezabel, Zadok, Jaddua,

units.leftText: Pelatiah, Hanan, Anaiah,
units.rightText: Pelatiah, Hanan, Anaiah,

units.leftText: Hoshea, Hananiah, Hasshub,
units.rightText: Hoshea, Hananiah, Hasshub,

units.leftText: Hallohesh, Pilha, Shobek,
units.rightText: Hallohesh, Pilha, Shobek,

units.leftText: Rehum, Hashabnah, Maaseiah,
units.rightText: Rehum, Hashabnah, Maaseiah,

units.leftText: Ahiah, Hanan, Anan,
units.rightText: Ahijah, Hanan, Anan,

units.leftText: Malluch, Harim, and Baanah.
units.rightText: Malluch, Harim, and Baanah.

units.leftText: The rest of the people, the priests, the Levites, the gatekeepers, the singers, the temple servants, and all those who had separated themselves from the peoples of the lands to the law of God, their wives, their sons, and their daughters—everyone who had knowledge and understanding—
units.rightText: “The rest of the people— the priests, Levites, gatekeepers, singers, temple servants, and all who had separated themselves from the people of the land to obey the Law of God— along with their wives and all their sons and daughters who are able to understand,
rightNotes: 10:28 Hebrew Nethinim

units.leftText: joined with their brothers, their nobles, and entered into a curse and into an oath, to walk in God’s law, which was given by Moses the servant of God, and to observe and do all the commandments of the LORD our Lord, and his ordinances and his statutes;
units.rightText: hereby join with their noble brothers and commit themselves with a sworn oath to follow the Law of God given through His servant Moses and to obey carefully all the commandments, ordinances, and statutes of the LORD our Lord.

units.leftText: and that we would not give our daughters to the peoples of the land, nor take their daughters for our sons;
units.rightText: We will not give our daughters in marriage to the people of the land, and we will not take their daughters for our sons.

units.leftText: and if the peoples of the land bring wares or any grain on the Sabbath day to sell, that we would not buy from them on the Sabbath, or on a holy day; and that we would forego the seventh year crops and the exaction of every debt.
units.rightText: When the people of the land bring merchandise or any kind of grain to sell on the Sabbath day, we will not buy from them on a Sabbath or holy day. Every seventh year we will let the fields lie fallow and will cancel every debt.

units.leftText: Also we made ordinances for ourselves, to charge ourselves yearly with the third part of a shekel for the service of the house of our God:
units.rightText: We also place ourselves under the obligation to contribute a third of a shekel yearly for the service of the house of our God:
leftNotes: 10:32 A shekel is about 10 grams or about 0.35 ounces.
rightNotes: 10:32 A third of a shekel is approximately 0.13 ounces or 3.8 grams, probably of silver.

units.leftText: for the show bread, for the continual meal offering, for the continual burnt offering, for the Sabbaths, for the new moons, for the set feasts, for the holy things, for the sin offerings to make atonement for Israel, and for all the work of the house of our God.
units.rightText: for the showbread, for the regular grain offerings and burnt offerings, for the Sabbath offerings, for the New Moons and appointed feasts, for the holy offerings, for the sin offerings to make atonement for Israel, and for all the duties of the house of our God.

units.leftText: We, the priests, the Levites, and the people, cast lots for the wood offering, to bring it into the house of our God, according to our fathers’ houses, at times appointed year by year, to burn on the LORD our God’s altar, as it is written in the law;
units.rightText: We have cast lots among the priests, Levites, and people for the donation of wood by our families at the appointed times each year. They are to bring it to the house of our God to burn on the altar of the LORD our God, as it is written in the Law.

units.leftText: and to bring the first fruits of our ground and the first fruits of all fruit of all kinds of trees, year by year, to the LORD’s house;
units.rightText: We will also bring the firstfruits of our land and of every fruit tree to the house of the LORD year by year.

units.leftText: also the firstborn of our sons and of our livestock, as it is written in the law, and the firstborn of our herds and of our flocks, to bring to the house of our God, to the priests who minister in the house of our God;
units.rightText: And we will bring the firstborn of our sons and our livestock, as it is written in the Law, and will bring the firstborn of our herds and flocks to the house of our God, to the priests who minister in the house of our God.

units.leftText: and that we should bring the first fruits of our dough, our wave offerings, the fruit of all kinds of trees, and the new wine and the oil, to the priests, to the rooms of the house of our God; and the tithes of our ground to the Levites; for they, the Levites, take the tithes in all our farming villages.
units.rightText: Moreover, we will bring to the priests at the storerooms of the house of our God the firstfruits of our dough, of our grain offerings, of the fruit of all our trees, and of our new wine and oil. A tenth of our produce belongs to the Levites, so that they shall receive tithes in all the towns where we labor.

units.leftText: The priest, the descendent of Aaron, shall be with the Levites when the Levites take tithes. The Levites shall bring up the tithe of the tithes to the house of our God, to the rooms, into the treasure house.
units.rightText: A priest of Aaron’s line is to accompany the Levites when they collect the tenth, and the Levites are to bring a tenth of these tithes to the storerooms of the treasury in the house of our God.

units.leftText: For the children of Israel and the children of Levi shall bring the wave offering of the grain, of the new wine, and of the oil, to the rooms where the vessels of the sanctuary are, and the priests who minister, with the gatekeepers and the singers. We will not forsake the house of our God.
units.rightText: For the Israelites and the Levites are to bring the contributions of grain, new wine, and oil to the storerooms where the articles of the sanctuary are kept and where the ministering priests, the gatekeepers, and the singers stay.

units.leftText: The princes of the people lived in Jerusalem. The rest of the people also cast lots to bring one of ten to dwell in Jerusalem, the holy city, and nine parts in the other cities.
units.rightText: Now the leaders of the people settled in Jerusalem, and the rest of the people cast lots to bring one out of ten to live in the holy city of Jerusalem, while the remaining nine were to dwell in their own towns.
rightNotes: 11:1 Hebrew nine hands

units.leftText: The people blessed all the men who willingly offered themselves to dwell in Jerusalem.
units.rightText: And the people blessed all the men who volunteered to live in Jerusalem.

units.leftText: Now these are the chiefs of the province who lived in Jerusalem; but in the cities of Judah, everyone lived in his possession in their cities—Israel, the priests, the Levites, the temple servants, and the children of Solomon’s servants.
units.rightText: These are the heads of the provinces who settled in Jerusalem. (In the villages of Judah, however, each lived on his own property in their towns— the Israelites, priests, Levites, temple servants, and descendants of Solomon’s servants—
rightNotes: 11:3 Hebrew Nethinim; also in verse 21

units.leftText: Some of the children of Judah and of the children of Benjamin lived in Jerusalem. Of the children of Judah: Athaiah the son of Uzziah, the son of Zechariah, the son of Amariah, the son of Shephatiah, the son of Mahalalel, of the children of Perez;
units.rightText: while some of the descendants of Judah and Benjamin settled in Jerusalem.)

units.leftText: and Maaseiah the son of Baruch, the son of Colhozeh, the son of Hazaiah, the son of Adaiah, the son of Joiarib, the son of Zechariah, the son of the Shilonite.
units.rightText: and Maaseiah son of Baruch, the son of Col-hozeh, the son of Hazaiah, the son of Adaiah, the son of Joiarib, the son of Zechariah, a descendant of Shelah.
rightNotes: 11:5 Or of the Shilonite

units.rightText: The descendants of Perez who settled in Jerusalem totaled 468 men of valor.

units.leftText: Of the priests: Jedaiah the son of Joiarib, Jachin,
units.rightText: From the priests:

units.rightText: Seraiah son of Hilkiah, the son of Meshullam, the son of Zadok, the son of Meraioth, the son of Ahitub, the chief official of the house of God;
