units.leftText: All the Levites in the holy city were two hundred eighty-four.
units.rightText: The Levites in the holy city totaled 284.

units.leftText: Moreover the gatekeepers, Akkub, Talmon, and their brothers, who kept watch at the gates, were one hundred seventy-two.
units.rightText: And the gatekeepers:

units.leftText: The residue of Israel, of the priests, and the Levites were in all the cities of Judah, everyone in his inheritance.
units.rightText: The rest of the Israelites, with the priests and Levites, were in all the villages of Judah, each on his own inheritance.

units.leftText: But the temple servants lived in Ophel; and Ziha and Gishpa were over the temple servants.
units.rightText: The temple servants lived on the hill of Ophel, with Ziha and Gishpa over them.

units.leftText: The overseer also of the Levites at Jerusalem was Uzzi the son of Bani, the son of Hashabiah, the son of Mattaniah, the son of Mica, of the sons of Asaph, the singers responsible for the service of God’s house.
units.rightText: Now the overseer of the Levites in Jerusalem was Uzzi son of Bani, the son of Hashabiah, the son of Mattaniah, the son of Mica. He was one of Asaph’s descendants, who were the singers in charge of the service of the house of God.
rightNotes: 11:22 Mica is a variant of Micaiah; see Nehemiah 12:35|NEH 12:35*.

units.leftText: For there was a commandment from the king concerning them, and a settled provision for the singers, as every day required.
units.rightText: For there was a command from the king concerning the singers, an ordinance regulating their daily activities.

units.leftText: Pethahiah the son of Meshezabel, of the children of Zerah the son of Judah, was at the king’s hand in all matters concerning the people.
units.rightText: Pethahiah son of Meshezabel, a descendant of Zerah son of Judah, was the king’s agent in every matter concerning the people.
rightNotes: 11:24 Hebrew hand

units.leftText: As for the villages with their fields, some of the children of Judah lived in Kiriath Arba and its towns, in Dibon and its towns, in Jekabzeel and its villages,
units.rightText: As for the villages with their fields, some of the people of Judah lived in Kiriath-arba, Dibon, Jekabzeel, and their villages;

units.leftText: in Jeshua, in Moladah, Beth Pelet,
units.rightText: in Jeshua, Moladah, and Beth-pelet;

units.leftText: in Hazar Shual, in Beersheba and its towns,
units.rightText: in Hazar-shual; in Beersheba and its villages;

units.leftText: in Ziklag, in Meconah and in its towns,
units.rightText: in Ziklag; in Meconah and its villages;

units.leftText: in En Rimmon, in Zorah, in Jarmuth,
units.rightText: in En-rimmon, Zorah, Jarmuth,

units.leftText: Zanoah, Adullam, and their villages, Lachish and its fields, and Azekah and its towns. So they encamped from Beersheba to the valley of Hinnom.
units.rightText: Zanoah, Adullam, and their villages; in Lachish and its fields; and in Azekah and its villages. So they settled from Beersheba all the way to the Valley of Hinnom.

units.leftText: The children of Benjamin also lived from Geba onward, at Michmash and Aija, and at Bethel and its towns,
units.rightText: The descendants of Benjamin from Geba lived in Michmash, Aija, and Bethel with its villages;

units.leftText: at Anathoth, Nob, Ananiah,
units.rightText: in Anathoth, Nob, Ananiah,

units.leftText: Hazor, Ramah, Gittaim,
units.rightText: Hazor, Ramah, Gittaim,

units.leftText: Hadid, Zeboim, Neballat,
units.rightText: Hadid, Zeboim, Neballat,

units.leftText: Lod, and Ono, the valley of craftsmen.
units.rightText: Lod, and Ono; and in the Valley of the Craftsmen.
rightNotes: 11:35 Hebrew in Ge-harashim

units.leftText: Of the Levites, certain divisions in Judah settled in Benjamin’s territory.
units.rightText: And some divisions of the Levites of Judah settled in Benjamin.

units.leftText: Now these are the priests and the Levites who went up with Zerubbabel the son of Shealtiel, and Jeshua: Seraiah, Jeremiah, Ezra,
units.rightText: Now these are the priests and Levites who went up with Zerubbabel son of Shealtiel and with Jeshua:

units.leftText: Amariah, Malluch, Hattush,
units.rightText: Amariah, Malluch, Hattush,
rightNotes: 12:2 Malluch is a variant of Malluchi; see verse 14.

units.leftText: Shecaniah, Rehum, Meremoth,
units.rightText: Shecaniah, Rehum, Meremoth,
rightNotes: 12:3 Rehum is a variant of Harim; see verse 15, Nehemiah 7:42|NEH 7:42*, and Ezra 2:39.

units.leftText: Iddo, Ginnethoi, Abijah,
units.rightText: Iddo, Ginnethon, Abijah,
rightNotes: 12:4 Many Hebrew manuscripts and Vulgate (see also verse 16); most MT manuscripts Ginnethoi

units.leftText: Mijamin, Maadiah, Bilgah,
units.rightText: Mijamin, Maadiah, Bilgah,
rightNotes: 12:5 Mijamin is a variant of Miniamin; see verse 17.
12:5 Maadiah is a variant of Moadiah; see verse 17.
12:5 Bilgah is a variant of Bilgai; also in verse 18; see Nehemiah 10:8|NEH 10:8*.

units.leftText: Shemaiah, Joiarib, Jedaiah,
units.rightText: Shemaiah, Joiarib, Jedaiah,

units.leftText: Sallu, Amok, Hilkiah, and Jedaiah. These were the chiefs of the priests and of their brothers in the days of Jeshua.
units.rightText: Sallu, Amok, Hilkiah, and Jedaiah.

units.leftText: Moreover the Levites were Jeshua, Binnui, Kadmiel, Sherebiah, Judah, and Mattaniah, who was over the thanksgiving songs, he and his brothers.
units.rightText: The Levites were Jeshua, Binnui, Kadmiel, Sherebiah, Judah, and Mattaniah, who, with his associates, led the songs of thanksgiving.

units.leftText: Also Bakbukiah and Unno, their brothers, were close to them according to their offices.
units.rightText: Bakbukiah and Unni, their associates, stood across from them in the services.

units.leftText: Jeshua became the father of Joiakim, and Joiakim became the father of Eliashib, and Eliashib became the father of Joiada,
units.rightText: Jeshua was the father of Joiakim,

units.leftText: and Joiada became the father of Jonathan, and Jonathan became the father of Jaddua.
units.rightText: Joiada was the father of Jonathan,
rightNotes: 12:11 Jonathan is a variant of Johanan; see verse 22.

units.leftText: In the days of Joiakim were priests, heads of fathers’ households: of Seraiah, Meraiah; of Jeremiah, Hananiah;
units.rightText: In the days of Joiakim, these were the heads of the priestly families:

units.leftText: of Ezra, Meshullam; of Amariah, Jehohanan;
units.rightText: of Ezra, Meshullam;

units.leftText: of Malluchi, Jonathan; of Shebaniah, Joseph;
units.rightText: of Malluchi, Jonathan;
rightNotes: 12:14 Malluchi is a variant of Malluch; see verse 2.

units.leftText: of Harim, Adna; of Meraioth, Helkai;
units.rightText: of Harim, Adna;

units.leftText: of Iddo, Zechariah; of Ginnethon, Meshullam;
units.rightText: of Iddo, Zechariah;

units.leftText: of Abijah, Zichri; of Miniamin, of Moadiah, Piltai;
units.rightText: of Abijah, Zichri;

units.leftText: of Bilgah, Shammua; of Shemaiah, Jehonathan;
units.rightText: of Bilgah, Shammua;

units.leftText: of Joiarib, Mattenai; of Jedaiah, Uzzi;
units.rightText: of Joiarib, Mattenai;

units.leftText: of Sallai, Kallai; of Amok, Eber;
units.rightText: of Sallai, Kallai;
rightNotes: 12:20 Sallai is a variant of Sallu; see verse 7.

units.leftText: of Hilkiah, Hashabiah; of Jedaiah, Nethanel.
units.rightText: of Hilkiah, Hashabiah;

units.leftText: As for the Levites, in the days of Eliashib, Joiada, Johanan, and Jaddua, there were recorded the heads of fathers’ households; also the priests, in the reign of Darius the Persian.
units.rightText: In the days of Eliashib, Joiada, Johanan, and Jaddua, during the reign of Darius the Persian, the heads of the families of the Levites and priests were recorded.
rightNotes: 12:22 Johanan is a variant of Jonathan; see verse 11.

units.leftText: The sons of Levi, heads of fathers’ households, were written in the book of the chronicles, even until the days of Johanan the son of Eliashib.
units.rightText: As for the descendants of Levi, the family heads up to the days of Johanan son of Eliashib were recorded in the Book of the Chronicles.
rightNotes: 12:23 Or the Book of the Annals or the Book of the Historical Events

units.leftText: The chiefs of the Levites: Hashabiah, Sherebiah, and Jeshua the son of Kadmiel, with their brothers close to them, to praise and give thanks according to the commandment of David the man of God, section next to section.
units.rightText: The leaders of the Levites were Hashabiah, Sherebiah, and Jeshua son of Kadmiel, along with their associates, who stood across from them to give praise and thanksgiving as one section alternated with the other, as prescribed by David the man of God.
rightNotes: 12:24 Or Sherebiah, Jeshua, Binnui, and Kadmiel

units.leftText: Mattaniah, Bakbukiah, Obadiah, Meshullam, Talmon, and Akkub were gatekeepers keeping the watch at the storehouses of the gates.
units.rightText: Mattaniah, Bakbukiah, Obadiah, Meshullam, Talmon, and Akkub were gatekeepers who guarded the storerooms at the gates.

units.leftText: These were in the days of Joiakim the son of Jeshua, the son of Jozadak, and in the days of Nehemiah the governor, and of Ezra the priest and scribe.
units.rightText: They served in the days of Joiakim son of Jeshua, the son of Jozadak, and in the days of Nehemiah the governor and Ezra the priest and scribe.
rightNotes: 12:26 Jozadak is a variant of Jehozadak; see 1 Chronicles 6:14|1CH 6:14*.

units.leftText: At the dedication of the wall of Jerusalem, they sought the Levites out of all their places, to bring them to Jerusalem to keep the dedication with gladness, both with giving thanks and with singing, with cymbals, stringed instruments, and with harps.
units.rightText: At the dedication of the wall of Jerusalem, the Levites were sought out from all their homes and brought to Jerusalem to celebrate the joyous dedication with thanksgiving and singing, accompanied by cymbals, harps, and lyres.

units.leftText: The sons of the singers gathered themselves together, both out of the plain around Jerusalem and from the villages of the Netophathites;
units.rightText: The singers were also assembled from the region around Jerusalem, from the villages of the Netophathites,

units.leftText: also from Beth Gilgal and out of the fields of Geba and Azmaveth, for the singers had built themselves villages around Jerusalem.
units.rightText: from Beth-gilgal, and from the fields of Geba and Azmaveth, for they had built villages for themselves around Jerusalem.

units.leftText: The priests and the Levites purified themselves; and they purified the people, the gates, and the wall.
units.rightText: After the priests and Levites had purified themselves, they purified the people, the gates, and the wall.

units.leftText: Then I brought the princes of Judah up on the wall, and appointed two great companies who gave thanks and went in procession. One went on the right hand on the wall toward the dung gate;
units.rightText: Then I brought the leaders of Judah up on the wall, and I appointed two great thanksgiving choirs. One was to proceed along the top of the wall to the right, toward the Dung Gate.
rightNotes: 12:31 Or alongside the wall; also in verse 38

units.leftText: and after them went Hoshaiah, with half of the princes of Judah,
units.rightText: Hoshaiah and half the leaders of Judah followed,

units.leftText: and Azariah, Ezra, and Meshullam,
units.rightText: along with Azariah, Ezra, Meshullam,

units.leftText: Judah, Benjamin, Shemaiah, Jeremiah,
units.rightText: Judah, Benjamin, Shemaiah, Jeremiah,

units.leftText: and some of the priests’ sons with trumpets: Zechariah the son of Jonathan, the son of Shemaiah, the son of Mattaniah, the son of Micaiah, the son of Zaccur, the son of Asaph;
units.rightText: and some of the priests with trumpets, and also Zechariah son of Jonathan, the son of Shemaiah, the son of Mattaniah, the son of Micaiah, the son of Zaccur, the son of Asaph,
rightNotes: 12:35 Micaiah is a variant of Mica; see Nehemiah 11:22|NEH 11:22*.

units.leftText: and his brothers, Shemaiah, Azarel, Milalai, Gilalai, Maai, Nethanel, Judah, and Hanani, with the musical instruments of David the man of God; and Ezra the scribe was before them.
units.rightText: and his associates— Shemaiah, Azarel, Milalai, Gilalai, Maai, Nethanel, Judah, and Hanani— with the musical instruments prescribed by David the man of God. Ezra the scribe led the procession.

units.leftText: By the spring gate, and straight before them, they went up by the stairs of David’s city, at the ascent of the wall, above David’s house, even to the water gate eastward.
units.rightText: At the Fountain Gate they went directly up the steps of the City of David on the ascent to the wall and passed above the house of David to the Water Gate on the east.

units.leftText: The other company of those who gave thanks went to meet them, and I after them, with the half of the people on the wall above the tower of the furnaces, even to the wide wall,
units.rightText: The second thanksgiving choir proceeded to the left, and I followed it with half the people along the top of the wall, past the Tower of the Ovens to the Broad Wall,

units.leftText: and above the gate of Ephraim, and by the old gate, and by the fish gate, the tower of Hananel, and the tower of Hammeah, even to the sheep gate; and they stood still in the gate of the guard.
units.rightText: over the Gate of Ephraim, the Jeshanah Gate, the Fish Gate, the Tower of Hananel, and the Tower of the Hundred, as far as the Sheep Gate. And they stopped at the Gate of the Guard.
rightNotes: 12:39 Or the Old City Gate

units.leftText: So the two companies of those who gave thanks in God’s house stood, and I and the half of the rulers with me;
units.rightText: The two thanksgiving choirs then stood in the house of God, as did I, along with the half of the officials accompanying me,

units.leftText: and the priests, Eliakim, Maaseiah, Miniamin, Micaiah, Elioenai, Zechariah, and Hananiah, with trumpets;
units.rightText: as well as the priests with their trumpets — Eliakim, Maaseiah, Miniamin, Micaiah, Elioenai, Zechariah, and Hananiah —

units.leftText: and Maaseiah, Shemaiah, Eleazar, Uzzi, Jehohanan, Malchijah, Elam, and Ezer. The singers sang loud, with Jezrahiah their overseer.
units.rightText: and also Maaseiah, Shemaiah, Eleazar, Uzzi, Jehohanan, Malchijah, Elam, and Ezer. Then the choirs sang out under the direction of Jezrahiah.

units.leftText: They offered great sacrifices that day, and rejoiced, for God had made them rejoice with great joy; and the women and the children also rejoiced, so that the joy of Jerusalem was heard even far away.
units.rightText: On that day they offered great sacrifices, rejoicing because God had given them great joy. The women and children also rejoiced, so that the joy of Jerusalem was heard from afar.

units.leftText: On that day, men were appointed over the rooms for the treasures, for the wave offerings, for the first fruits, and for the tithes, to gather into them according to the fields of the cities the portions appointed by the law for the priests and Levites; for Judah rejoiced for the priests and for the Levites who served.
units.rightText: And on that same day men were appointed over the rooms that housed the supplies, contributions, firstfruits, and tithes. The portions specified by the Law for the priests and Levites were gathered into these storerooms from the fields of the villages, because Judah rejoiced over the priests and Levites who were serving.

units.leftText: They performed the duty of their God and the duty of the purification, and so did the singers and the gatekeepers, according to the commandment of David and of Solomon his son.
units.rightText: They performed the service of their God and the service of purification, along with the singers and gatekeepers, as David and his son Solomon had prescribed.

units.leftText: For in the days of David and Asaph of old there was a chief of the singers, and songs of praise and thanksgiving to God.
units.rightText: For long ago, in the days of David and Asaph, there were directors for the singers and for the songs of praise and thanksgiving to God.

units.leftText: All Israel in the days of Zerubbabel and in the days of Nehemiah gave the portions of the singers and the gatekeepers, as every day required; and they set apart that which was for the Levites; and the Levites set apart that which was for the sons of Aaron.
units.rightText: So in the days of Zerubbabel and Nehemiah, all Israel contributed the daily portions for the singers and gatekeepers. They also set aside daily portions for the Levites, and the Levites set aside daily portions for the descendants of Aaron.

units.leftText: On that day they read in the book of Moses in the hearing of the people; and it was found written in it that an Ammonite and a Moabite should not enter into the assembly of God forever,
units.rightText: At that time the Book of Moses was read aloud in the hearing of the people, and in it they found the passage stating that no Ammonite or Moabite should ever enter the assembly of God,
rightNotes: 13:1 See Deuteronomy 23:3–6|DEU 23:3-6*.

units.leftText: because they didn’t meet the children of Israel with bread and with water, but hired Balaam against them to curse them; however, our God turned the curse into a blessing.
units.rightText: because they had not met the Israelites with food and water, but had hired Balaam to call down a curse against them (although our God had turned the curse into a blessing).

units.leftText: It came to pass, when they had heard the law, that they separated all the mixed multitude from Israel.
units.rightText: As soon as the people heard this law, they excluded from Israel all of foreign descent.

units.leftText: Now before this, Eliashib the priest, who was appointed over the rooms of the house of our God, being allied to Tobiah,
units.rightText: Now before this, Eliashib the priest, a relative of Tobiah, had been put in charge of the storerooms of the house of our God

units.leftText: had prepared for him a great room, where previously they laid the meal offerings, the frankincense, the vessels, and the tithes of the grain, the new wine, and the oil, which were given by commandment to the Levites, the singers, and the gatekeepers; and the wave offerings for the priests.
units.rightText: and had prepared for Tobiah a large room where they had previously stored the grain offerings, the frankincense, the temple articles, and the tithes of grain, new wine, and oil prescribed for the Levites, singers, and gatekeepers, along with the contributions for the priests.

units.leftText: But in all this, I was not at Jerusalem; for in the thirty-second year of Artaxerxes king of Babylon I went to the king; and after some days I asked leave of the king,
units.rightText: While all this was happening, I was not in Jerusalem, because I had returned to Artaxerxes king of Babylon in the thirty-second year of his reign. Some time later I obtained leave from the king
rightNotes: 13:6 Artaxerxes king of Persia is identified here as the king of Babylon because Persia had conquered the Babylonian Empire.

units.leftText: and I came to Jerusalem, and understood the evil that Eliashib had done for Tobiah, in preparing him a room in the courts of God’s house.
units.rightText: to return to Jerusalem. Then I discovered the evil that Eliashib had done on behalf of Tobiah by providing him a room in the courts of the house of God.

units.leftText: It grieved me severely. Therefore I threw all Tobiah’s household stuff out of the room.
units.rightText: And I was greatly displeased and threw all of Tobiah’s household goods out of the room.

units.leftText: Then I commanded, and they cleansed the rooms. I brought into them the vessels of God’s house, with the meal offerings and the frankincense again.
units.rightText: Then I ordered that the rooms be purified, and I had the articles of the house of God restored to them, along with the grain offerings and frankincense.

units.leftText: I perceived that the portions of the Levites had not been given them, so that the Levites and the singers, who did the work, had each fled to his field.
units.rightText: I also learned that because the portions for the Levites had not been given to them, all the Levites and singers responsible for performing the service had gone back to their own fields.

units.leftText: Then I contended with the rulers, and said, “Why is God’s house forsaken?” I gathered them together, and set them in their place.
units.rightText: So I rebuked the officials and asked, “Why has the house of God been neglected?”

units.leftText: Then all Judah brought the tithe of the grain, the new wine, and the oil to the treasuries.
units.rightText: and all Judah brought a tenth of the grain, new wine, and oil into the storerooms.

units.leftText: I made treasurers over the treasuries, Shelemiah the priest, and Zadok the scribe, and of the Levites, Pedaiah: and next to them was Hanan the son of Zaccur, the son of Mattaniah; for they were counted faithful, and their business was to distribute to their brothers.
units.rightText: I appointed as treasurers over the storerooms Shelemiah the priest, Zadok the scribe, and Pedaiah of the Levites, with Hanan son of Zaccur, the son of Mattaniah, to assist them, because they were considered trustworthy. They were responsible for distributing the supplies to their fellow Levites.

units.leftText: Remember me, my God, concerning this, and don’t wipe out my good deeds that I have done for the house of my God, and for its observances.
units.rightText: Remember me for this, O my God, and do not blot out my deeds of loving devotion for the house of my God and for its services.

units.leftText: In those days I saw some men treading wine presses on the Sabbath in Judah, bringing in sheaves, and loading donkeys with wine, grapes, figs, and all kinds of burdens which they brought into Jerusalem on the Sabbath day; and I testified against them in the day in which they sold food.
units.rightText: In those days I saw people in Judah treading winepresses on the Sabbath and bringing in grain and loading it on donkeys, along with wine, grapes, and figs. All kinds of goods were being brought into Jerusalem on the Sabbath day. So I warned them against selling food on that day.

units.leftText: Some men of Tyre also lived there, who brought in fish and all kinds of wares, and sold on the Sabbath to the children of Judah, and in Jerusalem.
units.rightText: Additionally, men of Tyre who lived there were importing fish and all kinds of merchandise and selling them on the Sabbath to the people of Judah in Jerusalem.

units.leftText: Then I contended with the nobles of Judah, and said to them, “What evil thing is this that you do, and profane the Sabbath day?
units.rightText: Then I rebuked the nobles of Judah and asked, “What is this evil you are doing— profaning the Sabbath day?

units.leftText: Didn’t your fathers do this, and didn’t our God bring all this evil on us and on this city? Yet you bring more wrath on Israel by profaning the Sabbath.”
units.rightText: Did not your forefathers do the same things, so that our God brought all this disaster on us and on this city? And now you are rekindling His wrath against Israel by profaning the Sabbath!”

units.leftText: It came to pass that when the gates of Jerusalem began to be dark before the Sabbath, I commanded that the doors should be shut, and commanded that they should not be opened until after the Sabbath. I set some of my servants over the gates, so that no burden should be brought in on the Sabbath day.
units.rightText: When the evening shadows began to fall on the gates of Jerusalem, just before the Sabbath, I ordered that the gates be shut and not opened until after the Sabbath. I posted some of my servants at the gates so that no load could enter on the Sabbath day.

units.leftText: So the merchants and sellers of all kinds of wares camped outside of Jerusalem once or twice.
units.rightText: Once or twice, the merchants and those who sell all kinds of goods camped outside Jerusalem,

units.leftText: Then I testified against them, and said to them, “Why do you stay around the wall? If you do so again, I will lay hands on you.” From that time on, they didn’t come on the Sabbath.
units.rightText: but I warned them, “Why are you camping in front of the wall? If you do it again, I will lay hands on you.” From that time on, they did not return on the Sabbath.

units.leftText: I commanded the Levites that they should purify themselves, and that they should come and keep the gates, to sanctify the Sabbath day. Remember me for this also, my God, and spare me according to the greatness of your loving kindness.
units.rightText: Then I instructed the Levites to purify themselves and guard the gates in order to keep the Sabbath day holy.

units.leftText: In those days I also saw the Jews who had married women of Ashdod, of Ammon, and of Moab;
units.rightText: In those days I also saw Jews who had married women from Ashdod, Ammon, and Moab.

units.leftText: and their children spoke half in the speech of Ashdod, and could not speak in the Jews’ language, but according to the language of each people.
units.rightText: Half of their children spoke the language of Ashdod or of the other peoples, but could not speak the language of Judah.

units.leftText: I contended with them, cursed them, struck certain of them, plucked off their hair, and made them swear by God, “You shall not give your daughters to their sons, nor take their daughters for your sons, or for yourselves.
units.rightText: I rebuked them and called down curses on them. I beat some of these men and pulled out their hair.

units.leftText: Didn’t Solomon king of Israel sin by these things? Yet among many nations there was no king like him, and he was loved by his God, and God made him king over all Israel. Nevertheless foreign women caused even him to sin.
units.rightText: Did not King Solomon of Israel sin in matters like this? There was not a king like him among many nations, and he was loved by his God, who made him king over all Israel— yet foreign women drew him into sin.

units.leftText: Shall we then listen to you to do all this great evil, to trespass against our God in marrying foreign women?”
units.rightText: Must we now hear that you too are doing all this terrible evil and acting unfaithfully against our God by marrying foreign women?”

units.leftText: One of the sons of Joiada, the son of Eliashib the high priest, was son-in-law to Sanballat the Horonite; therefore I chased him from me.
units.rightText: Even one of the sons of Jehoiada son of Eliashib the high priest had become a son-in-law to Sanballat the Horonite. Therefore I drove him away from me.

units.leftText: Remember them, my God, because they have defiled the priesthood and the covenant of the priesthood and of the Levites.
units.rightText: Remember them, O my God, because they have defiled the priesthood and the covenant of the priesthood and of the Levites.

units.leftText: Thus I cleansed them from all foreigners and appointed duties for the priests and for the Levites, everyone in his work;
units.rightText: Thus I purified the priests and Levites from everything foreign, and I assigned specific duties to each of the priests and Levites.

units.leftText: and for the wood offering, at appointed times, and for the first fruits. Remember me, my God, for good.
units.rightText: I also arranged for contributions of wood at the appointed times, and for the firstfruits.
